standard_prerequisites.name: Homotopy initial algebras
standard_prerequisites.statement: A natural-number algebra is homotopy initial when the type of algebra homomorphisms from it to any other such algebra is contractible.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the hypothesis of the statement and the source of the two homomorphisms used in the proof.

standard_prerequisites.name: Contractibility of a hom-type
standard_prerequisites.statement: In a contractible type any two elements are equal, and the type is inhabited.
standard_prerequisites.use: It produces the two homomorphisms between the two algebras and makes their composites equal to the identities.

standard_prerequisites.name: Univalence and mere propositions
standard_prerequisites.statement: An equivalence of types gives an equality of them by univalence, and a type is a mere proposition when its identity types are contractible.
standard_prerequisites.use: It turns the exhibited equivalence into the equality of the algebras and transfers the set-level claim to the property of being h-initial.

core_obligations: Take two h-initial algebras and use the contractibility of the hom-types between them to obtain a homomorphism in each direction (source lines 439-440).

Show that the composite of the two homomorphisms is the identity, using that the hom-type from the first algebra to itself is contractible and that the composite and the identity are both elements of it (source line 441).
Do the same in the other order to obtain the other round-trip identity and hence an equivalence of the two algebras (source line 442).

Apply univalence to get the equality of the algebras, then conclude that being h-initial is a mere proposition, because contractibility is a mere proposition and dependent products preserve mere propositions (source line 443).

proof_roadmap.step: Two homomorphisms out of the contractibility of the hom-types.
Both composites are the identities by contractibility of the endomorphism hom-types.
Univalence gives the equality; the set-level claim follows from the propositional character of the ingredients.
